newsitem.title: USA: Dollar soars against Swiss franc in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars against Swiss franc in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: The dollar climbed Tuesday to its highest level against the Swiss franc in more than two years on worries about the weak economy in Switzerland.
The dollar rose against the yen after another drop in Japanese stocks and gained ground against most other major currencies in light trading on the day before Christmas.
Financial markets in the United States and Europe will be closed for Christmas Wednesday. Trading reopens in France and the United States on Thursday and in other major European markets Friday.

The Swiss National Bank has already cut a key interest rate to 1 percent to help boost that nation's struggling economy. The central bank also vowed this month not to raise rates until clear signs of an economic recovery emerged.
Low rates hurt the franc by making deposits denominated in that currency less attractive to investors.
Diego Giurleo, vice president of the Treasury at Royal Bank of Canada, said the Swiss are looking to stimulate growth by increasing demand for Swiss-made exports.

"And to get growth out of the export sector, one of the major tools is to get a more competitive currency, which means a weaker currency," Giurleo said. A weaker franc cheapens the cost of Swiss exports.
The dollar surged to 1.3465 francs, the highest since September 1994. In late trading, the dollar settled at 1.3455 francs, up from 1.3373 francs on Monday.
The dollar rose to 1.5565 German marks from 1.5545 marks late Monday. Against the Japanese currency, the dollar climbed to 114.47 yen from 114.08 yen Monday.

The bulk of the dollar's gains against the yen came overnight after Tokyo's Nikkei index of 225 stocks tumbled 528.75 points or 2.69 percent to 19,161.71, its lowest in a year. The drop in stock fed mounting fears that foreign investors selling Japanese securities would weigh on the yen.
"This is a concern that an underpeforming equity market is not going to continue to attract foreign investors," said Alex Beuzelin, a foreign exchange trader at Ruesch International.

"So, what you're seeing is maybe some flight out of Japanese equities markets," Beuzelin said. "Obviously, when they are doing this, they need to sell their Japanese yen and that puts some pressure on the yen."
Although the dollar gained ground against the yen, the American currency failed to hit its high for the year of 114.92 yen, reached in late October.
"You're not going to see full volume in trading resume until after the new year," Beuzelin said.
The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3650 from C$1.3666 late on Monday. The British pound fell to $1.6725 from $1.6775.
